propositions: The undecomposed hard-override axis fires on 0.1% of verified findings (11/10,250 plan-v3, 18/11,773 plan-v4) but carries full impact-floor power (any non-none grade floors to 0.85), making low grades equivalent to high grades.
The stated G5 deterministic suppressor (cited as justification for low fire rate) is inert: it never fired across 2,000 reviews and is inapplicable to 91%+ of the corpus (childless tickets).
The axis' non-none grades drove impact floors in 25 of 29 verified fires as the sole hard-override criterion present, and at least one low-grade finding blocked due to the floor alone.

The inverse population (findings with text matching undecomposed regex but scored none) contains 33 plan-v3 and 17 plan-v4 matches; sampled inspection shows these are regex false positives on code-decomposition language, not missed plan defects.

The undecomposed axis suffers the same miscalibration previously fixed for ac_unverifiable and divergent_implementation: ordinal-ladder grades (low/medium/high) mapped uniformly to a hard floor, conflating severity levels.
